How I Did It: Knight Flyer

by Sal, Galaxy Zone Arcade

Sal remembers the original cabinet

Joust came in '82, right in the thick of the golden years, and I swear it caused more arguments than any machine I ever owned — two people, two buttons each, flapping like fools, and whoever's ostrich was standing a half-inch higher won the whole fight. I had a regular named Trudy who'd talk trash the entire match and then lose to her own little brother because she flew too low chasing him into the lava. He never let her forget it. I never let either of them forget the quarters they owed the jar.

What the remodel changed

The height rule was always the whole game, so the crew made sure it still is — whoever's mount is higher wins the joust, dead even and you just bounce off each other. What's new is everything got weight to it. Gravity pulls you down every single tick, so a "flap" isn't holding a button, it's a real timed press, one push, one lift, and you'd better time the next one. They gave the lava a grab — dip too low and a hand comes up for you, and only fast flapping gets you out of it. And I finally got that pterodactyl to behave the way I remembered it: show up when you're dawdling, and punish you for it unless you fly right at it with the lance forward.

The spell that did it

Build Joust against our GZ engine. One button press should be one flap — no holding it down — with real gravity pulling me back down between flaps, and momentum for left/right in the air. Joust rule stays the same: higher mount wins, dead-even bounces off. Give me a lava pit at the bottom that grabs me if I skim it unless I flap my way out fast. Defeated riders drop an egg I can collect, but leave it too long and it hatches into something tougher. And if I take too long clearing a wave, send in the pterodactyl.

Under the hood

  • Flap is edge-triggered — it fires exactly once per physical press no matter how long you hold the button — while gravity keeps adding downward speed every dt regardless.
  • Landing only counts one direction: falling onto a platform's top stops you, but you can fly straight up through the underside, same as the original never punished you for popping up through a ledge.
  • An egg remembers which tier of rider laid it, so when it hatches late it comes back one rung meaner — bounder becomes hunter, hunter becomes a shadow lord.
  • The pterodactyl only dies to a head-on hit — if you're drifting the same direction it's charging, or standing still, it's your mount that goes down instead.
